repos.name: wide-world-importers
repos.notes: Only the wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt subtree of the sql-server-samples monorepo is cloned locally (the full monorepo is unrelated samples and far larger than needed). Full multi-schema business-app DDL: tables, views, functions, procs across Application/Sales/Purchasing/Warehouse/Security schemas. No CREATE DATABASE statement in the SSDT project itself, but wwi-ssdt/wwi-ssdt/WideWorldImporters.sqlproj declares <DefaultCollation>Latin1_General_100_CI_AS</DefaultCollation> directly - this is the collation SSDT deploys the database with, not a guess.

repos.name: dnn-platform
repos.notes: 339 .SqlDataProvider files (DNN Platform/Website/Providers/DataProviders/SqlDataProvider/ plus per-module Providers/DataProviders/SqlDataProvider/ under DNN Platform/Modules/*). DDL and stored procedures are interleaved in the same incremental-upgrade files, not split into separate table/proc paths, hence the identical globs. IMPORTANT: files use {databaseOwner}/{objectQualifier} template tokens (by convention 'dbo.' and '' respectively) that must be substituted before ScriptDOM can parse them - see templateSubstitutions below. Collation left unpinned on purpose, not merely unresearched: no CREATE/ALTER DATABASE COLLATE statement anywhere in the checked-in DDL, no collation requirement documented in README/BUILD docs, and only 12 of thousands of string columns across the whole corpus carry an explicit per-column COLLATE (8 SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, 4 Latin1_General_CI_AS - both families appear, so even that thin sample doesn't point one way). DNN predates any single documented target collation (its DotNetNuke lineage goes back to SQL Server 2000-era installs); the study reports this repo's varchar/nvarchar findings under both collation-family assumptions rather than picking one.

repos.name: sql-server-first-responder-kit
repos.notes: Root-level scripts, each a single large stored procedure (sp_Blitz, sp_BlitzCache, sp_BlitzIndex, sp_BlitzFirst, sp_BlitzWho, sp_BlitzLock, sp_DatabaseRestore, etc.) built with idempotent IF OBJECT_ID(...) IS NULL EXEC('CREATE PROCEDURE ... AS RETURN 0;') then ALTER PROCEDURE pattern, plus heavy dynamic SQL construction. Same list for ddl/proc paths since scripts mix incidental table creation with the procedure body. Install-All-Scripts.sql and Install-Azure.sql are deliberately excluded from both lists (an audit finding): they're generated concatenations of every individual script above, not independent content - including them alongside the individual files triple-counted every procedure's predicates in prevalence figures, since TypedFindingDeduplicator collapses the resulting duplicate FINDINGS but the summary's classified-comparison denominator was never deduplicated. Collation left unpinned as a positive finding, not an unresearched gap: these are DBA diagnostic scripts meant to install into ANY customer database regardless of its collation, and the source is explicit about that - every temp-table string column is declared COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT (IndexOptimize-style tables aren't present here, but Uninstall.sql's COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT join and sp_DatabaseRestore.sql's own comment ('COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2 is required so the LIKE pattern catches NCHAR(0) - under default collations the NUL byte is silently dropped') both show the authors deliberately coding around an unknown target collation. Pinning one here would misrepresent a tool that's collation-agnostic by design.

repos.name: ola-hallengren-maintenance-solution
repos.notes: Root-level scripts (CommandLog.sql, Queue.sql, QueueDatabase.sql, DatabaseBackup.sql, DatabaseIntegrityCheck.sql, IndexOptimize.sql, CommandExecute.sql). CommandLog.sql/Queue.sql/QueueDatabase.sql contain real CREATE TABLE DDL; the rest are large parameterized stored procedures. Widely deployed in production DBA shops. MaintenanceSolution.sql and MaintenanceSolutionAzureSQLDatabase.sql are deliberately excluded (an audit finding, same pattern as the First Responder Kit entry above): both are generated all-in-one installers that embed the identical CREATE PROCEDURE bodies from DatabaseBackup.sql/IndexOptimize.sql/DatabaseIntegrityCheck.sql/CommandExecute.sql verbatim (verified: `CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[DatabaseBackup] AS` appears in both DatabaseBackup.sql and MaintenanceSolution.sql), not independent content - including them would multiply-count the same predicates in prevalence figures. Collation left unpinned as a positive finding, not an unresearched gap: IndexOptimize.sql declares every temp-table string column (#SelectedIndexes, #Info, #ExistingObjects, and more) COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT explicitly, because this maintenance solution installs into and operates against arbitrary customer databases whose collation isn't known at authoring time. Pinning one would misrepresent a tool that's collation-agnostic by design.

repos.name: mojoportal
repos.notes: Fork of the original mojoPortal.org CMS, still maintained. dev3CreateStoredProcedures.sql wraps its CREATE PROCEDURE statements as string literal arguments to EXEC dbo.sp_executesql (idempotent-create pattern), which CLAUDE.md's dynamic SQL policy says is parseable in principle (single string literal, no concatenation) - a good real-world exercise of that rule, distinct from the other 4 repos' plain top-level DDL. mojoPortal.Data.MSSQL/legacyscripts/ contains older upgrade deltas, intentionally excluded here in favor of the dev*.sql full-install scripts. These 4 files are genuinely this repo's ENTIRE standalone-.sql surface, not an under-scoped glob (an audit finding, checked directly): mojoPortal.Data.MSSQL/ and mojoPortal.Features.Data.MSSQL/ contain no other .sql files at all - the rest of this repo's SQL lives as string literals embedded inside its ADO.NET data-access .cs files (DBBlog.cs, DBEvents.cs, etc.), which is out of this tool's SQL-text-only v1 scope (CLAUDE.md hard scope: ScriptDOM parses T-SQL, not C#-embedded SQL string extraction - a materially different problem from the EXEC/sp_executesql dynamic SQL this tool does handle, since here the SQL never appears as a T-SQL literal ScriptDOM can parse at all, only as a C# string this tool has no C# parser for). Widening the glob would not surface more content; there is none to surface without a C#-string-extraction pass this project does not have. Collation genuinely unresearched, not a positive finding either way: mojoPortal.Data.MSSQL/legacyscripts/1CreateDatabase.sql's CREATE DATABASE has no COLLATE clause (inherits whatever the target SQL Server instance's own default is), and no install doc in this repo states a required collation - unlike DNN/First Responder Kit/Ola Hallengren, there was no positive evidence either pinning a value or explaining why one is deliberately absent.
